confounds.name: Differences across data sources bias comparisons

experiment_recipes.goal: Verify official CIFAR-10 splits are used with zero train/test leakage
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Report official splits exactly and prevent leakage — Use the benchmark’s official train/val/test (or class-exclusive zero-shot) splits and document them; ensure no overlap (e.g., mutually exclusive classes for zero-shot, patient-level splits in medical)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if and only if: (1) |train| == 50000 and |test| == 10000; and (2) the intersection size between the sets of SHA-256 hashes of all train images and all test images is exactly 0. Otherwise, refute.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Confirms adherence to the field’s requirement of using official, non-overlapping splits; any leakage refutes standard practice immediately.

experiment_recipes.goal: Build and validate a standard supervised CIFAR-10 classifier with held-out validation, proper normalization/augmentation, and logged curves
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Use held-out validation and/or cross-validation for hyperparameters and early stopping — Reserve a validation split or perform CV to select learning rates/regularization and stop training based on validation metrics
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train ResNet on CIFAR-10 with a 10% held-out validation split (exactly 5000 images). Pass if and only if: (1) validation split size == 5000; (2) per-epoch training and validation loss are logged for all configured epochs (count of logged epochs equals configured epochs); (3) the selected best epoch by minimum validation loss occurs strictly before the final epoch; and (4) test Top-1 accuracy >= 93.5%. Otherwise, refute.
depends_on: Verify official CIFAR-10 splits are used with zero train/test leakage
experiment_recipes.rationale: Establishes a credible, reproducible apparatus that follows standard practice (held-out validation, normalization/augmentation, optimizer schedule) and reaches a recognized CIFAR-10 baseline.

experiment_recipes.goal: Quantify and report the effect of training augmentations versus a no-augmentation baseline
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Document data augmentation — Report training augmentations (e.g., random resized crop/aspect/area ranges, flips, AutoAugment, CutMix) and any traditional augmentations used for baselines
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train two runs under identical settings except augmentations: (A) standard CIFAR-10 aug (random crop with padding=4, horizontal flip) and (B) no augmentation. Pass if and only if (Top-1_Augmented − Top-1_NoAugmented) ≥ 3.0 percentage points on the CIFAR-10 test set. Otherwise, refute.
depends_on: Build and validate a standard supervised CIFAR-10 classifier with held-out validation, proper normalization/augmentation, and logged curves
experiment_recipes.rationale: Demonstrates the widely accepted impact of augmentations and the need to document them; a substantial delta is expected under standard practice.

experiment_recipes.goal: Evaluate and report test-time augmentation and ensembling effects under a specified protocol
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Test-time augmentation and ensembling protocol — Describe test-time crops/scales/flips and how predictions are averaged across augmentations and models
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using the same architecture and training as the apparatus, evaluate: (1) single-model, single-view; (2) single-model with test-time horizontal flip averaging; (3) 3-model ensemble (different random seeds) with the same TTA averaging. Pass if and only if: (i) TTA improves single-model Top-1 by ≥ 0.1 percentage points; and (ii) the 3-model ensemble improves over the best single-model (with the same TTA) by ≥ 0.3 percentage points. Otherwise, refute.
depends_on: Build and validate a standard supervised CIFAR-10 classifier with held-out validation, proper normalization/augmentation, and logged curves
experiment_recipes.rationale: Verifies that TTA/ensembling are explicitly defined and have measurable impact, aligning with standard reporting practice.

experiment_recipes.goal: Confirm PR is computed via threshold sweeps (not a single confusion matrix) on a multi-label benchmark
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Precision-Recall evaluation protocol — Compute PR curves by varying decision thresholds (not from a single confusion matrix) and report AUPRC where appropriate
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Compute per-class PR curves by sweeping thresholds in [0,1] and AUPRC per class. Also compute scikit-learn average_precision_score per class and a naive PR area from a single 0.5 threshold confusion matrix. Pass if and only if: (1) for every class, |AUPRC_sweep − AP_sklearn| ≤ 1e-3; and (2) the naive single-threshold PR area underestimates AUPRC_sweep by ≥ 5% relative on at least 5 classes. Otherwise, refute.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Establishes compliance with the field’s PR evaluation norm and exposes the inadequacy of single-threshold PR estimates, guarding against a common evaluation pitfall.
